sights.w: Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 645) — through the Kaminarimon thunder gate and the Nakamise-dōri stall street to the main hall and five-storey pagoda.

sights.n: Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館)
sights.w: Japan's oldest and largest museum — 120,000 objects including 89 National Treasures, from Jōmon pottery to samurai armour and ukiyo-e, in Ueno Park.
Japan's first public park (1873) — museums, the zoo, Shinobazu Pond's lotus beds, Tōshō-gū and Tokyo's most famous cherry-blossom avenue. Free entry.
'Kitchen Town' — some 170 shops between Ueno and Asakusa selling knives, lacquerware, noren and the plastic food samples of every Japanese shop window.
The national sumo hall — three of the six annual grand tournaments (January, May, September) are fought here; the Sumo Museum and the chanko-nabe restaurants of Ryōgoku surround it.

sights.n: Sumida Hokusai Museum (すみだ北斎美術館)
sights.w: Kazuyo Sejima's faceted aluminium museum (2016) for Hokusai, who spent most of his 88 years in Sumida — his life, his prints and the neighbourhood that shaped them.
Meiji-era stroll garden built by the Iwasaki (Mitsubishi) family — a big pond, stepping stones of prized rock from across Japan, carp, turtles and a lakeside teahouse.
Edo-period shrine in old-town Yanesen with a tunnel of small vermilion torii and a hillside of some 3,000 azaleas each April.

sights.n: Shibuya Scramble Crossing (渋谷スクランブル交差点)
sights.w: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing — up to 3,000 people per green light outside Shibuya Station and the Hachikō statue; watch it from Shibuya Sky or the station's upper floors.
Big, informal park beside Meiji Jingū — weekend buskers, rockabilly dancers, ginkgo avenues in autumn and festivals on the event plaza.

sights.n: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (新宿御苑)
sights.w: Former imperial garden blending French formal, English landscape and Japanese styles — 1,000 cherry trees, a tropical greenhouse and a teahouse, minutes from Shinjuku Station.

sights.n: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (東京都庁)
sights.w: Kenzo Tange's twin-towered city hall with free 202 m observation decks — Mt Fuji on clear winter mornings and an evening projection-mapping show on the facade.

sights.n: Shinjuku Golden Gai (新宿ゴールデン街)
sights.w: Six narrow lanes of 200-odd postwar shoebox bars, each seating a handful — the most atmospheric drinking quarter in Tokyo.
Shrine to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken in a 70-hectare planted forest between Harajuku and Yoyogi — giant cypress torii, sake-barrel wall, and Japan's busiest New Year hatsumōde.

sights.n: Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー)
sights.w: At 634 m the world's tallest tower — observation decks at 350 m and 450 m, with Tokyo Solamachi mall and an aquarium at its foot.
